query: AlCrFeNiSi belongs to a high-entropy-alloy family developed to combine properties that traditional single-principal-element alloys often cannot achieve simultaneously. Earlier research sought stable solid solutions and adjusted HEA compositions to target particular properties, but tradeoffs persisted: the CoCrFeMnNi system has limited wear and corrosion resistance, manganese can promote oxidation and oxide spallation, and cobalt-containing systems raise cost and processability concerns. Conventional bulk fabrication can cause compositional segregation during cooling, whereas mainstream metallic additive-manufacturing techniques can generate residual thermal stresses that impair mechanical performance and increase processing complexity. Given cobalt-free AlCrFeNiSi powder feedstock, what single intervention could improve mechanical integrity while limiting segregation, residual stress, and defect formation? State one hypothesis containing the intervention, its causal mechanism, a quantitative or directional outcome relative to conventionally fabricated AlCrFeNiSi, the processing and test boundaries of validity, the prior evidence supporting it, and a decisive experiment that could falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: Incorporating a small amount (≈0.5–1 wt.%) of nanometer-scale oxide particles (e.g., Y2O3) into cobalt‐free AlCrFeNiSi powder feedstock during laser additive manufacturing will promote heterogeneous nucleation, refine grain size, and restrict deleterious silicon segregation and residual stress buildup, thereby enhancing mechanical integrity relative to the conventional, unmodified process.
generation.material_initial_state: Cobalt‐free AlCrFeNiSi powder feedstock produced by mechanical alloying or atomization.
generation.intervention: Pre-mix the AlCrFeNiSi powder with a controlled dispersion of nanoparticles (e.g., 0.5–1 wt.% Y2O3) prior to laser additive manufacturing.
generation.conditions: Process samples via a standard laser powder bed fusion or directed energy deposition setup under typical energy density and cooling rate conditions for this alloy; experiments conducted over a range of nanoparticle additions around the target percentage to identify optimal conditions.
generation.structural_mediator: The uniformly dispersed oxide particles act as heterogeneous nucleation sites that promote rapid grain refinement and pin growing grain boundaries, limiting local elemental diffusion that leads to silicon segregation, as well as moderating the evolution of residual stresses.
generation.mechanism: The nano-oxides facilitate a higher nucleation rate during solidification, resulting in a finer and more uniform microstructure. This refined microstructure inhibits prolonged solute diffusion, reducing elemental segregation (especially of silicon) and redistributes thermal stresses more evenly, thereby diminishing residual stress accumulation and defect formation.
generation.predicted_outcome: Compared to conventionally processed samples, the nanoparticle–modified builds will exhibit a finer grain structure, reduced silicon segregation, lower residual stress levels (measured by e.g., XRD or EBSD kernel average misorientation), and an improved mechanical integrity evidenced by higher yield strength and ductility.
generation.baseline: AlCrFeNiSi components produced via laser additive manufacturing from unmodified powder feedstock.
generation.boundary: This effect is expected under typical additive manufacturing conditions (high cooling rates and steep thermal gradients) for cobalt‐free AlCrFeNiSi and with nanoparticle additions not exceeding approximately 1 wt.%; extrapolation beyond these processing conditions and composition variations remains untested.
generation.uncertainty: This hypothesis extends findings from studies on dispersion strengthening (such as in DS-MEAs where Y2O3 pins grain boundaries, PMC7296023::web::008) and observations that rapid melting–solidification in systems like AlCoCrFeNiSi (PMC5849017::web::025) yield uniform microstructures. What is new here is applying a tailored nanoparticle inoculant strategy to mitigate silicon segregation and residual stress specifically in cobalt‐free AlCrFeNiSi during AM. The quantitative balance between nanoparticle concentration and the targeted degree of grain refinement is uncertain and requires optimization.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of samples via laser additive manufacturing using cobalt‐free AlCrFeNiSi powder: one set with the optimized nanoparticle (Y2O3) addition (≈0.5–1 wt.%) and a control set without nanoparticles. Maintain all other processing parameters identical. Characterize the microstructure using SEM/EBSD and elemental mapping (e.g. EDS) to quantify grain size and silicon segregation; measure residual stress via XRD or EBSD kernel average misorientation; and conduct standardized tensile tests to evaluate mechanical properties.
measurements: Residual stress levels (XRD residual stress measurements, EBSD KAM)
Mechanical properties (yield strength, ultimate tensile strength, elongation)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the nanoparticle-modified samples do not show statistically significant improvements in grain refinement, reduced silicon segregation, lower residual stress, and enhanced mechanical performance compared to the control samples, then the hypothesis is falsified.

Obvious difference can be found upon comparing the XRD pattern of the coating with that of the feedstock powder. As mentioned above (Figure 7), the powder milled for 10 h was composed of BCC, FCC, and a small amount of Fe, Cr, and Si elemental phases. After plasma spraying, besides the matrix BCC phase, an ordered BCC phase was detected. In addition, the peak intensity of the FCC phase increased, while the diffraction peaks of the Si elemental phase disappeared. These results indicate that phase transformation occurred during plasma spraying. Figure 10 shows the cross-sectional microstructure of the APS AlCoCrFeNiSi coating. From Figure 10a,b, it can be seen that a coating with a thickness of about 220 μm was obtained. Besides a few obvious near-spherical pores with dimensions of less than 10 μm, the microstructure of the coating was dense and uniform.
